procedures.title: Residence registration for foreigners arriving from abroad (Cambio di residenza per persone straniere provenienti dall'estero)
facts: The request is made online: download the forms and documents, attach them to the online application, then submit.
Legal effects of the registration start from the date the declaration is submitted; the City then checks the requirements (if checks fail, the procedure stops and the applicant can reply).
Non-EU applicants attach both sides of the valid residence permit, or the expired permit plus the renewal receipt (YesMilano).

procedures.title: Change of residence / address (Cambio di residenza)
facts: For people coming from another Italian comune or moving within Milan; done on the national registry site (ANPR) with SPID or CIE.
The move must be declared to the Registry Office within 20 days.
Registration happens within two working days of the declaration; the City then verifies the requirements.

procedures.title: TARI waste tax: declaration of occupation of a flat (Tari: dichiarazione di occupazione)
facts: Anyone who starts occupying a flat or room must file a TARI occupation declaration; it can be done online ('Dichiara occupazione').
The declared data affect the TARI bill from the two-month period after the one in which occupation started.

Alternatives: PEC to tassarifiuti@pec.comune.milano.it, e-mail to tassarifiuti@comune.milano.it, by hand at the Protocollo, or registered post to Servizio Tassa Rifiuti, via Silvio Pellico 16, 20121 Milano.
Deadline: the team's research reports 90 days from the start of occupation (City TARI regulation); this page does not state it, so tell the user to confirm on the page.

procedures.title: TARI payment (Tari: pagamento)
facts: Wait for the payment notice (by post or in the Fascicolo del Cittadino) before paying; due dates are on the notice.
Payment is via pagoPA; direct debit can be requested.

procedures.title: Electronic identity card (Carta d'identità, CIE)
facts: Book an appointment online to get or renew the CIE at a registry office (booking: https://servizicrm.comune.milano.it/Appuntamenti/AnagrafeCIE).
Bring the health card (Tessera sanitaria) or tax code, and a recent colour passport photo on a light background; some registry offices have certified photo booths.
Only residents can get it: register your residence first (YesMilano).

procedures.title: Registry certificates (Certificati anagrafici)
facts: Certificates can be requested online (Fascicolo del Cittadino) or at the counter by appointment.
An appointment is needed for certificates for third parties and for some certificate types.

procedures.title: Fascicolo del Cittadino (citizen's online file)
facts: Access with SPID or CIE.
Shows registry data (ID card, residence permit), lets you request certificates, pay TARI with pagoPA, see your occupation declarations and track City appointments.
Before you have SPID/CIE (which need a tax code, and the CIE needs residence) you cannot use it.

procedures.title: Rent contribution for young workers (Contributo sostegno affitto per giovani lavoratori)
facts: One-off contribution up to EUR 2,400 to cover rent only (no extra charges).
Requirements include being under 35 and an ISEE up to EUR 26,000; funds go by order of application until exhausted.

procedures.title: Milano Abitare (below-market rent agency)
facts: City agency matching people whose income is too high for public housing but too low for market rents with below-market (canone calmierato) homes.

procedures.title: Which municipio is my street in? (In che municipio è via...)
facts: Official lookup to find the municipio (1-9) of an address; use it to pick the registry office of the user's municipio.

procedures.title: Registry offices: appointments and infoline
facts: All registry counters work by online appointment only; urgent tickets are issued until 30 minutes before closing (ds549 notes).
City infoline: 020202.

procedures.title: Residence permit for study (Permesso di soggiorno)
facts: Non-EU students must apply for the residence permit within 8 working days of arriving in Italy.

procedures.title: Tax code (Codice fiscale)
facts: Free and valid for life; students already in Italy request it at the Agenzia delle Entrate (6 offices in Milan) with form AA4/8.

procedures.title: Student transport pass (ATM)
facts: First buy the ATM card (EUR 10, valid 4 years) online or at an ATM Point, then load the student fare; book ATM Point via the ATM app.

procedures.title: Free Italian courses
facts: Schools of Italian for foreigners and CPIA (public adult schools) are listed with address, levels and free/paid flag in dataset ds551: use find_places kind=scuola_italiano.
